tasks.title: Mutation-testing scaffold (mutmut, pilot-first)
tasks.verification_command: mutmut run && mutmut results --all true (with pyproject.toml's [tool.mutmut] config)
tasks.oracle_tier_actually_executed: real pilot run in a python:3.12-slim container against src/libipynb/codec/writer.py (the smallest of the 4 hot modules, per this taskcard's own pilot-first mandate): 268 mutants, 186 killed, 61 survived, 21 no-tests, 75.3% score (killed/(killed+survived)). Pilot went through 3 real structural incompatibility classes before reaching a working state, each fixed via mutmut's own intended mechanism rather than forced around: (1) 3 tests asserting libipynb's import origin IS site-packages, structurally incompatible with mutmut's copy-and-mutate execution model -- deselected individually; (2) 2 tests reading repo-root files (.gitlab-ci.yml, scripts/fetch_fixture.py, plans/state.json) mutmut's mutants/ tree doesn't copy by default -- fixed via also_copy for the 2 simple files, the 2 requiring nested directories (plans/state.json, scripts/fetch_fixture.py -- also_copy uses shutil.copy2, which does not create intermediate directories) had their owning test files ignored instead, since both are governance/script metadata orthogonal to writer.py's own behavior; (3) THE load-bearing fix: pytest-cov (installed transitively via the test extra) auto-registers as a pytest plugin and conflicts with mutmut's own internal coverage.py instrumentation, making every single mutant report '<no tests>' (pytest exit code 5) regardless of real coverage -- fixed with `-p no:cov`, confirmed by re-running and getting real kill/survive results immediately after. A second real bug was caught and fixed in the accompanying mutation.yml CI workflow before commit: `mutmut results` with no flag silently omits killed mutants from its output by default (only showing survived/no-tests), which would have made the score-gate script always compute killed=0 and always fail -- fixed with `mutmut results --all true`, verified against the real 268-mutant dataset (186/61/21, exactly matching the pilot run) before committing.

tasks.title: v3->v4 legacy notebook import (decision-gated)
tasks.verification_command: pytest tests/unit/test_doc_drift.py -v --tb=short (no drift check exists for this specific decision beyond README consistency)
tasks.note: DECISION: EXCLUDE native v3 import, per the mission's own explicit 'unless evidence justifies inclusion' default posture. Investigation performed before deciding, not skipped: (1) confirmed directly against the installed nbformat==5.10.4 package that nbformat 4 has been Jupyter's default format since 2015 (over a decade before this writing) -- nbformat.current_nbformat == 4; (2) confirmed nbformat itself still ships and maintains the full v1->v2->v3->v4 upgrade chain (nbformat.v3.upgrade, nbformat.read(as_version=4)) specifically for this legacy case; (3) empirically verified the escape hatch actually works, not just assumed: constructed a real, structurally-plausible nbformat v3 document (worksheets/cells/prompt_number-shaped, the genuine legacy schema, not a guess) and confirmed nbformat.reads(src, as_version=4) correctly auto-upgrades it to nbformat 4.5 with cells translated correctly. Given (a) any actively-maintained v3 notebook would already have been auto-upgraded by Jupyter itself over the last decade, making genuine new v3 input vanishingly rare, and (b) the reference implementation this project already treats as its own schema/oracle authority (nbformat) already solves this exact problem and is a natural, low-friction escape hatch, re-implementing v3 parsing natively here would duplicate an already-solved, low-value problem rather than add real capability. Documented in README.md's 'Supported Versions' section (new paragraph + a working code example) rather than left as a silent gap.

tasks.title: 67 real-kernel tests in tests/integration/test_obligation_jupyter_execution_adapter.py are never run with a provisioned kernel in any real CI job, and 3 fail under real container timing when they are
tasks.objective: Discovered by LIBIPYNB-Q22's independent Taskcard-Gate-G2 review: this file's own docstring says it is 'not skipped by default: CI must install the exec extra plus ipykernel for this file to prove anything,' but no real CI job actually does that for it. test-py311/312/313 (the jobs that run tests/integration/) extend .python-base, whose before_script installs only .[test] -- no jupyter_client/nbclient at all, so this file's module-level pytest.importorskip trips unconditionally and all 67 tests collapse to a single skip. oracle-and-package (the only job LIBIPYNB-Q22 taught to provision a kernel) runs pytest tests/oracle/ tests/package/ -v --tb=short -- it never touches tests/integration/. The '1056 passed' local evidence cited throughout this engagement (LIBIPYNB-Q16-Q22) counts these 67 as real passes only because this dev .venv already has ipykernel and a registered python3 kernelspec from unrelated prior work -- nothing tracked in the repo provisions that, so real CI has no such state. When the reviewer provisioned exec+kernel in a fresh python:3.12-slim container matching the CI image and ran this file there, 3 of the 67 tests FAILED with container-timing-sensitive 'Timeout waiting for execute reply (1s)' errors (test_interrupt_on_timeout_true_reports_the_timeout_as_a_cell_error, test_concurrent_runs_on_separate_threads_do_not_interfere, test_multiple_independently_timed_out_cells_are_each_recorded) -- so wiring this suite into CI is not a risk-free follow-up; the timing assumptions themselves need investigation first. ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE (2026-08-24, this session, unrelated to any src/ change -- confirmed via `git diff <last-Phase-1-commit>..HEAD --stat -- src/` returning empty): a 4th test in the same file, test_stopped_early_and_timed_out_can_both_be_true_for_the_same_run, failed reproducibly (both in a full local run and in isolation, on this session's own Windows dev machine, not a Linux container) with `record.error.ename == 'KeyboardInterrupt'` instead of the expected `'RuntimeError'` -- the same general real-kernel interrupt/timeout race-classification fragility this card already tracks, now confirmed on a second, unrelated platform/mechanism (genuine system contention on a heavily-loaded shared host, not container-specific timing), broadening rather than duplicating this finding.

tasks.title: codec/writer.py's LIBIPYNB-Q31 mutation baseline surfaced 61 survived mutants and a real coverage gap in roundtrip()
tasks.objective: LIBIPYNB-Q31's mutation-testing pilot (mutmut==3.7.0, scoped to src/libipynb/codec/writer.py) recorded a real, working baseline: 268 mutants, 186 killed, 61 survived, 21 no-tests (75.3% score, killed/(killed+survived)). Two distinct, actionable findings, deliberately not fixed as part of Q31 itself (whose own scope is the tooling/scaffold, not exhaustively closing every gap it surfaces): (1) ALL 21 of roundtrip()'s mutants show 'no tests' (pytest exit code 5 scoped to that function specifically), meaning mutmut's coverage-based test selection found literally no test that exercises any mutated line of roundtrip() at all -- either a genuine, total coverage gap for this one public function, or a narrower structural mutmut-vs-this-function interaction worth confirming either way, not assumed. (2) 61 survived mutants across _as_mapping, _profile_version, _normalized, dumps, dump, and _resolve_destination -- each one a real, specific behavioral change to writer.py that the CURRENT test suite does not catch, despite writer.py's own line/branch coverage sitting at 97% (coverage.py) -- direct, concrete evidence that line/branch coverage alone materially understates real test strength for this module, the same thesis the governing plan's own diagnosis section (test-authoring habits missing >=2-item interactions) already established via a different mechanism.
